reasons.C: Closest sentence movement: short declaratives and verbless fragments in a flat, plain, first-person manner, concrete and unhedged, no colons; only slightly heavier on fragment runs than the passage.
reasons.A: Short sentences and fragments fit, but it drifts into instructional explanation with commas and subordinate clauses ('If you leave old grout...', 'which is another reason') more than the author does.
reasons.B: Short sentences, but it leans on stock phrasing and small flourishes ('the hard way', 'It always is', 'Every time') and a neat rounded ending, which the author's dry, unadorned stance avoids.
reasons.D: Long, comma-chained and colon-led sentences, explanatory essay register and a moralising close; the opposite of the author's clipped rhythm and plain diction.
